subject: AWS Offer: Inference Runtime — finalize product page copy and billing CTA
messages:
From: Amrita Singh <amrita.singh@scaleops.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: AWS listing copy for Inference Runtime (need CTA + billing clarity)

Sean — thanks for the call earlier. Attached is our draft AWS Offer page and a short pricing matrix. Two things we really need to lock down before submission to the marketplace team:

1) The product page hero/three-bullet copy — want it concise but accurate for field demos.
2) The billing CTA and trial flow — do we list pay-as-you-go pricing on the public product page or steer users to a Private Offer (30-day trial) CTA? Customers ask for transparent pricing but our sales motion prefers a Private Offer for enterprise trials.

Can you confirm Redwood's recommendation and send suggested wording for the hero and the CTA? Also, if there are any disallowed claims we should avoid on the page (latency/uptime language), call them out.

Attachment: inference_runtime_offer_draft.pdf (1 page)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync after you and your team review.
— Amrita
Product & Partnerships | ScaleOps

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 10:02:18 -0700
Subject: FW: Draft: AWS listing copy for Inference Runtime (need CTA + billing clarity)

Folks — forwarding ScaleOps' draft (attached). They want finalized product page copy and a clear recommendation on public pricing vs private offer trial CTA. Timeline: can we turn initial edits back to me by 12:00 PT so I can share with Amrita and loop AWS PM (Tom) by 1pm?

Kimberly: hero + 3 bullets + CTA phrasing (two options: pay-as-you-go snippet and Private Offer trial copy).
Olga: AMI/technical claims and compliance-friendly sentence (SOC2/KMS notes). Avoid any hard latency numbers unless we can map to an SLA.
Marissa: short field playbook blurb (1 paragraph) for co-sell listing — how sales should position trial.

Attachments: inference_runtime_offer_draft.pdf

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 11:05:34 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Draft: AWS listing copy for Inference Runtime (need CTA + billing clarity)

Sean — quick pass below. I kept options short so we can A/B in the listing or pick what's best once ScaleOps confirms trial flow.

--- Suggested hero (short):
Inference Runtime — Low-latency model serving for production applications

Alternative (more benefit-led):
Inference Runtime — Serve large language models at predictable cost and latency

Three bullets (condensed):
• Optimized GPU runtime with continuous batching and KV cache for predictable per-token cost.
• Deploy on Redwood Dedicated or via AWS Marketplace with private offers and VPC options.
• Integrated rollout and rollback policies with observability for production apps.

CTA options (pick one):
A) Public page (transparent): 
"Start pay-as-you-go — see pricing tiers and estimated cost per 1M tokens" (link to pricing table)
B) Private Offer (recommended for enterprise trials):
"Request a 30-day private offer trial — contact us to enable your account and reserve capacity"

Pricing footnote suggestion: "Actual costs depend on model selection, sequence length, and provisioned capacity. Contact Redwood for private-offer pricing and regional availability."

Notes: avoid absolute latency claims (e.g., "sub-100ms") unless legal has a vetted SLA. Also avoid the phrase "unlimited throughput."

Uploading a short doc with copy variants and a simple pricing scenarios spreadsheet.

Attachments: inference_runtime_aws_offer_draft.docx, pricing-scenarios.xlsx

— Kim
Senior Product Marketing Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Amrita Singh <amrita.singh@scaleops.com>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@amazon.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Draft: AWS listing copy for Inference Runtime (need CTA + billing clarity)

Hi Amrita and Tom — thanks for the draft. We've consolidated copy and a recommended CTA below. See attached final offer page draft and pricing scenarios.

Finalized product page copy (concise):
Hero: Inference Runtime — Serve large language models with predictable cost and production controls
Bullets:
• GPU-optimized serving with continuous batching, KV cache, and quantization-friendly execution
• Deploy via AWS Marketplace (Private Offer for trials) or Redwood Dedicated for reserved capacity
• Built-in rollout, observability, and automatic fallback policies for reliability

Recommended CTA (recommended):
Request a 30-day private offer trial — contact us to enable your account and reserve capacity

Optional public pricing line (if you want a transparent starter):
Pay-as-you-go pricing available — view pricing tiers and estimate your cost per 1M tokens

Compliance-friendly sentence for AMI/technical section (from Olga):
Redwood supports customer-managed VPCs, BYOK KMS integrations, and provides audit logs suitable for SOC 2 readiness.

Field playbook blurb (from Marissa):
For co-sell/field: position the Private Offer trial as the recommended path for enterprise evaluation — include a short demo of the runtime using a 10–20 minute sample workload and share the pricing scenarios spreadsheet during the procurement conversation.

Next steps:
• Amrita: please confirm whether ScaleOps prefers we list a public pay-as-you-go price or route prospects to a Private Offer trial.
• Tom: if AWS Marketplace team needs any changes to the offer metadata, please advise.

Attachments: inference_runtime_aws_offer_draft.docx, pricing-scenarios.xlsx

If everyone is OK, we will submit the offer page copy to Marketplace by EOD and set the Private Offer flow as the default CTA for enterprise trials.

Best —
Sean Gallagher
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
